A data analyst who only sees the output cannot increase the privacy loss.

Running them independently and releasing all outputs, $x \mapsto \prod_i M_i(x)$, is $\big(\sum_i \varepsilon_i, \sum_i \delta_i\big)$-differentially private: "the epsilons and the deltas add up". nodes.summary: A mechanism $M$ is $\varepsilon$-differentially private if and only if $M(x) \le e^{\varepsilon} M(y)$ as measures for all neighbours $x, y$. This form is what makes pure differential privacy pass through integrals: $\int f \, dM(x) \le e^{\varepsilon} \int f \, dM(y)$ for every nonnegative measurable $f$.
nodes.title: Pure differential privacy as a measure inequality

For a neighbouring relation $\mathrm{Adj}$ on databases, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\delta \in [0, \infty]$, the mechanism is $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-differentially private if for all $x, y$ with $\mathrm{Adj}(x, y)$ and every measurable $S \subseteq \Omega$,
nodes.title: Differential privacy

nodes.summary: Let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}^d$ have $\ell_2$-sensitivity at most $\Delta_2 \ge 0$, i.e. $\|f(x) - f(y)\|_2 \le \Delta_2$ for all neighbours. Let $\varepsilon \in (0, 1)$, $\delta > 0$, $c > 0$ with $c^2 > 2\ln(1.25/\delta)$, and $\sigma \ge c\Delta_2/\varepsilon$. Releasing $f(x) + Z$ with $Z \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I_d)$ is $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-differentially private. Calibrating to the $\ell_2$ rather than the…
nodes.title: The Gaussian mechanism

nodes.summary: If $M$ is $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-differentially private with $\varepsilon \ge 0$, then along a chain of $k$ neighbouring steps $M(z_0)(S) \le e^{k\varepsilon} M(z_k)(S) + k e^{(k-1)\varepsilon}\delta$: the mechanism is $(k\varepsilon, k e^{(k-1)\varepsilon}\delta)$-differentially private for groups of size $k$. The additive term "takes a big hit", unlike the pure case.
nodes.title: Group privacy, approximate case

nodes.summary: If $M$ is $\varepsilon$-differentially private for neighbouring histograms, then for all histograms with $\|x - y\|_1 \le k$ and every measurable $S$, $M(x)(S) \le e^{k\varepsilon} M(y)(S)$. Two histograms at $\ell_1$ distance at most $k$ are joined by a chain of at most $k$ single-record changes, to which group privacy along a chain applies.
nodes.title: Group privacy for histograms

nodes.title: Group privacy along a chain

nodes.summary: A database of $n$ rows from a set $U$ is a list $S : \{0, \dots, n - 1\} \to U$. Two such databases are neighbours when they differ in at most one row, i.e. their Hamming distance is at most $1$. This is the relation used for data sets of i.i.d. samples, for instance in adaptive data analysis.
nodes.title: Neighbouring row databases

nodes.summary: A database over a finite universe $U$ of record types is a histogram $x : U \to \mathbb{N}$, where $x(u)$ counts the records of type $u$. Two histograms are neighbours when $\|x - y\|_1 = \sum_{u} |x(u) - y(u)| \le 1$: they differ by adding or removing at most one record.
nodes.title: Neighbouring histograms

nodes.summary: If $M$ is $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-differentially private and $f : \Omega \to \Omega'$ is measurable, then $x \mapsto f_* M(x)$ is $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-differentially private. For an event $S \subseteq \Omega'$ apply the definition to the preimage $T = f^{-1}(S)$.
nodes.title: Post-processing by a measurable map

nodes.summary: An $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-differentially private mechanism is $(\varepsilon', \delta')$-differentially private whenever $\varepsilon \le \varepsilon'$ and $\delta \le \delta'$: the bound $M(x)(S) \le e^{\varepsilon} M(y)(S) + \delta$ only weakens.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the privacy parameters

nodes.summary: If $M_1$ is $(\varepsilon_1, \delta_1)$-differentially private and $M_2$ is $(\varepsilon_2, \delta_2)$-differentially private, both with values in probability measures, then releasing both with independent coins is $(\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2, \delta_1 + \delta_2)$-differentially private.
nodes.title: Composition of approximate differential privacy, two mechanisms

nodes.summary: If $M_1$ is $\varepsilon_1$-differentially private and $M_2$ is $\varepsilon_2$-differentially private (with $s$-finite output laws), then releasing both, with independent coins, $x \mapsto M_1(x) \otimes M_2(x)$, is $(\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2)$-differentially private.
nodes.title: Composition of pure differential privacy

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
